column3: Verify that the navigation menu remains functional after updates.
column4:
1. Access https://www.boost.org. 
2. Click each navigation menu item (e.g., Libraries, Documentation, Downloads, Community). 
3. If dropdowns exist, hover and click sub-items. 
4. Check URLs and page content.
column5: All menu items redirect to the correct pages with no 404 errors. Dropdowns function as before, and content matches expectations (e.g., Libraries shows a list).
column7: High-priority due to navigation being critical. Compare with pre-update behavior.

column3: Ensure library documentation is unchanged after content migration.
column4:
1. Navigate to the Libraries page. 
2. Select two libraries (e.g., Boost.Asio, Boost.Beast). 
3. Verify documentation sections (overview, examples, API reference). 
4. Compare content with boost.org for equivalence. 
5. Test a code example’s copy functionality.
column5: Documentation matches boost.org content, includes all sections, and code examples are copyable. No content is missing or altered unexpectedly.
column7: High-priority due to documentation’s importance. Manually verify examples (e.g., HTTP SSL client).

column3: Confirm that search performance and accuracy are unaffected by updates.
column4:
1. Access the search bar. 
2. Enter previously tested queries (e.g., “Boost.Asio”, “WebSocket”). 
3. Submit and observe results. 
4. Measure load time. 
5. Click a result to verify redirection.
column5: Results are consistent with prior tests, load within 3 seconds, and are relevant. Clicking a result redirects to the correct page.
column7: High-priority for developer usability. Test multiple queries to ensure no degradation.

column3: Verify that download links and instructions remain functional post-update.
column4:
1. Navigate to the Downloads page. 
2. Click the link for the latest Boost release. 
3. Verify the download starts. 
4. Check for instructions (e.g., OpenSSL prerequisites). 
5. Test a previous release link.
column5: Downloads start immediately, files match expected size/format, and instructions are unchanged. Previous release links work as before.
column7: High-priority for user access. Verify file integrity for both releases.

column3: Ensure community links and features are unaffected by updates.
column4:
1. Navigate to the Community page. 
2. Click links to GitHub issues and mailing lists. 
3. If a form (e.g., newsletter signup) exists, submit a valid email. 
4. Test with an invalid email.
column5: Links open in new tabs and are valid (e.g., https://github.com/boostorg/website-v2/issues). Form submissions show expected success/error messages, consistent with prior behavior.
column7: Medium priority but important for engagement. Re-test all external links.

column3: Confirm that the logo displays correctly after redesign or optimization.
column4:
1. Access the homepage. 
2. Inspect the logo image. 
3. Verify file size (< 500 KB) and dimensions.
4. Check for visual clarity (no pixelation). 
5. Compare with community feedback (e.g., no “SS” or “Gatorade” resemblance).
column5: Logo loads correctly, is optimized, and appears clear. It matches the approved design and avoids community-reported issues.
column7: Medium priority but critical due to community feedback. Test on high-resolution displays.

column3: Ensure no new rendering issues across browsers post-update.
column4:
1. Open https://www.boost.org on Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. 
2. Navigate to homepage, Libraries, and Downloads. 
3. Check layout, text, and button alignment. 
4. Test search and navigation.
column5: The website renders consistently across browsers, with no new misalignments or broken elements. Functionality matches prior tests.
column7: High-priority for user access. Use BrowserStack to compare with pre-update screenshots.

column3: Verify that mobile usability is unchanged after updates.
column4:
1. Open https://www.boost.org on a mobile device (e.g., iPhone 12, Samsung Galaxy S21). 
2. Check homepage layout and navigation (e.g., hamburger menu). 
3. Access a documentation page. 
4. Perform a search.
column5: Layout adjusts correctly, navigation is accessible, documentation is readable, and search works as before. No new usability issues.
column7: High-priority due to mobile usage. Test on both iOS and Android.

column3: Confirm that page load times are unaffected by updates.
column4:
1. Measure load times for homepage, Libraries, and Downloads pages using a tool (e.g., Chrome DevTools). 
2. Compare with pre-update benchmarks. 
3. Test under low-bandwidth conditions.
column5: Load times remain within 2 seconds for normal conditions and are comparable to pre-update performance. Site is usable under low bandwidth.
column7: Medium priority but critical for user experience. Log any degradation for optimization.

column3: Ensure error handling (e.g., 404 pages) remains functional.
column4:
1. Navigate to an invalid URL (e.g., https://www.boost.org/nonexistent). 
2. Observe the response. 
3. If forms exist, submit invalid data (e.g., incorrect email). 
4. Check error messages.
column5: A user-friendly 404 page is displayed for invalid URLs. Forms show appropriate error messages for invalid inputs, consistent with prior behavior.
column7: Medium priority but important for UX. Test multiple invalid URLs and form inputs.
